title: Chapter 127 — The Deck
paragraphs: The coffin lies on two line-tubs between the vise-bench and the open hatchway; the Carpenter is caulking its seams, the strand of twisted oakum slowly unwinding from a large roll of it tucked into the front of his smock. Ahab comes slowly from the cabin-gangway and hears Pip following him.
"Back, lad; I'll be with you again soon. He goes! This hand of mine does not do my bidding more kindly than that boy does. — Middle aisle of a church! What's here?"
"Life-buoy, sir. Mr. Starbuck's orders. Oh, look, sir! Beware the hatchway!"
"Thank you, man. Your coffin lies handy to the vault."
"Sir? The hatchway? Oh! So it does, sir, so it does."
"Aren't you the leg-maker? Look, didn't this stump come from your shop?"
"I believe it did, sir; does the ferrule stand, sir?"
"Well enough. But aren't you also the undertaker?"
"Aye, sir; I patched this thing together as a coffin for Queequeg, but now they've set me to turning it into something else."

"Then tell me: aren't you an arrant, all-grasping, intermeddling, monopolizing, heathenish old scamp, to be one day making legs, and the next day coffins to clap them in, and yet again life-buoys out of those same coffins? You are as unprincipled as the gods, and as much of a jack-of-all-trades."
"But I do not mean anything, sir. I do as I do."

"The gods again. Listen, don't you ever sing while working on a coffin? The Titans, they say, hummed snatches of song when chipping out the craters for volcanoes; and the grave-digger in the play sings, spade in hand. Don't you ever?"

"Sing, sir? Do I sing? Oh, I'm indifferent enough for that, sir; but the reason the grave-digger made music must have been that there was none in his spade, sir. The caulking mallet, though, is full of it. Listen to it."

"Aye, and that's because the lid there is a sounding-board; and what makes the sounding-board in all things is this — there's nothing beneath. And yet a coffin with a body in it rings pretty much the same, carpenter. Have you ever helped carry a bier, and heard the coffin knock against the churchyard gate, going in?"
"Faith, sir, I've —"
"Faith? What's that?"
"Why, faith, sir, it's only a sort of exclamation-like — that's all, sir."
"Um, um; go on."
"I was about to say, sir, that —"
"Are you a silk-worm? Do you spin your own shroud out of yourself? Look at your bosom! Be quick! and get these traps out of sight."

"He goes aft. That was sudden, now; but squalls come sudden in hot latitudes. I've heard that the Isle of Albemarle, one of the Galapagos, is cut by the Equator right in the middle. Seems to me some sort of Equator cuts that old man, too, right in his middle. He's always under the Line — fiery hot, I tell you! He's looking this way — come, oakum; quick. Here we go again. This wooden mallet is the cork, and I'm the professor of musical glasses — tap, tap!"
(Ahab to himself.)

"There's a sight! There's a sound! The gray-headed woodpecker tapping the hollow tree! The blind and the dumb might well be envied now. Look! That thing rests on two line-tubs full of tow-lines. A most malicious joker, that fellow. Rat-tat! So man's seconds tick! Oh, how immaterial all materials are! What real things are there, except weightless thoughts? Here now is the very dreaded symbol of grim death, turned by mere chance into the expressive sign of help and hope for life in the greatest danger. A life-buoy made of a coffin! Does it go further? Can it be that, in some spiritual sense, the coffin is after all only an immortality-preserver? I'll think about that. But no. I am so far gone into the dark side of the earth that its other side, the theoretical bright one, seems only an uncertain twilight to me. Will you never be done, Carpenter, with that cursed sound? I'm going below; don't let me see that thing here when I come back. Now then, Pip, we'll talk this over; I suck the most wondrous philosophies out of you! Some unknown channels from the unknown worlds must empty into you!"
